title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
description:
`heights[r][c]` gives the height of a cell. The Pacific Ocean touches the top row and left column; the Atlantic Ocean touches the bottom row and right column. Water in a cell can flow to an adjacent cell (up, down, left, right) whose height is **less than or equal** to its own, and any border cell can drain into the ocean next to it.

Return every coordinate `[r, c]` from which water can reach **both** oceans, in any order.

examples.explanation: The only cell touches both oceans.

hints: Simulating flow from every cell separately repeats a lot of work. Think about starting at the oceans instead.
Reverse the direction: from the ocean border cells, climb to neighbours that are equal or higher.
Run one search from all Pacific border cells and one from all Atlantic border cells, each recording reachable cells. The answer is the intersection of the two sets.

solution.explanation: Water that can run from a cell to an ocean can be traced backwards: starting at the ocean's border cells, move to neighbours that are equal or higher. Do one traversal seeded with the top row and left column (Pacific) and one seeded with the bottom row and right column (Atlantic), each marking reachable cells. Cells in both sets are the answer. Each traversal visits each cell once, so O(m*n) time and space, versus O((m*n)^2) for flowing from every cell.
solution.code:
class Solution:
    def pacificAtlantic(self, heights: List[List[int]]) -> List[List[int]]:
        rows, cols = len(heights), len(heights[0])

        def reach(starts):
            seen = set(starts)
            stack = list(starts)
            while stack:
                r, c = stack.pop()
                for nr, nc in ((r + 1, c), (r - 1, c), (r, c + 1), (r, c - 1)):
                    if (0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols and (nr, nc) not in seen
                            and heights[nr][nc] >= heights[r][c]):
                        seen.add((nr, nc))
                        stack.append((nr, nc))
            return seen

        pac = [(0, c) for c in range(cols)] + [(r, 0) for r in range(1, rows)]
        atl = [(rows - 1, c) for c in range(cols)] + [(r, cols - 1) for r in range(rows - 1)]
        both = reach(pac) & reach(atl)
        return [[r, c] for r, c in sorted(both)]
